Subject: Trail tips for your next stretch — plus a word from us
CTA: Read more on the Northbay trail blog -> https://www.northbaysupply.com/blog/trail-tips
Body: Hey,

You've been out there lately, so we'll keep this useful.

---

**Three trail tips worth revisiting this season:**

**1. Recheck your base-layer weight.**
Midseason conditions shift fast. If you're packing a 200-weight fleece for shoulder-season starts, consider whether a 150-weight would cover your actual temperature range without the extra 3–4 oz. Small margins add up over a full day.

**2. Water carry: plan for the dry stretches, not the wet ones.**
Most trip-planning errors happen when hikers route by map miles, not water availability. If a segment runs 8 miles between reliable sources, carry capacity for at least 10 miles. Thirst slows pace more than pack weight does.

**3. Break in footwear on similar terrain.**
Broken-in trail runners on flat paths don't tell you much about rocky descents. Put 10–15 miles on new footwear over terrain that resembles your target route before committing to a long push.

---

**A note from us:**

This is a meaningful season for Northbay Supply. We're introducing a new direction in our gear lineup — built around the specific feedback you and our broader community have given us over the past two years. It's a step we've taken deliberately, not quickly. We'll share the details soon.

For now: get your miles in. We'll have more to show you shortly.

— The Northbay Supply team
